title: Check yourself: MCP: hosts, clients, servers and the three primitives

questions.stem: An AI application connects to a ticketing system and a document store, both exposed through MCP. How is the connecting side organized?

options.text: One shared client multiplexes both servers over one connection
options.says: Ruled out because each client "maintains a dedicated connection with its corresponding MCP server", so none is shared.

options.text: The host talks to each server itself, with no client component
options.says: Ruled out because "The host does not talk to a server itself."

options.text: Each server creates a client inside itself to call back
options.says: Ruled out because it is the host that does the creating: "The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server".

options.text: The host creates one client for each server
options.says: The page says "The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server", and that each client "maintains a dedicated connection with its corresponding MCP server".

questions.stem: A server publishes a read-only database schema, and the host app chooses when to attach it to the model's context. Which primitive does this describe?

options.text: A tool, which the model decides to call
options.says: Ruled out because a tool is one of the "Functions that the model can call", not passive data.

options.text: A prompt, which a person picks from a menu
options.says: Ruled out because "Prompts are picked by a person, for example from a menu", and here the application, not a person, chooses.

options.text: A resource, which the application accesses directly
options.says: A schema is data that the application attaches, and the page says a resource gives "read-only access to information, such as a file or a database schema" which the application "can access this information directly and decide how to use it".

options.text: A sampling request, which the server sends to the client
options.says: Ruled out because sampling is the case where "the server asks the client's model for a completion", which moves no data to the model's context.

questions.stem: How does a client written for the 2026-07-28 revision tell a server which protocol version it speaks?

options.text: An initialize exchange that opens a session and fixes it for later calls
options.says: Ruled out because the legacy versions "establish a session with an initialize handshake", and the modern ones have none.

options.text: A header on the first call only, which the server remembers afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because the server "accepts or rejects each request independently", so nothing is remembered from a first call.

options.text: Each call carries it in its metadata field, with no opening handshake
options.says: The page says "Every request declares the protocol version it is using" in its metadata field, and that the server "accepts or rejects each request independently".

options.text: A mandatory discovery call that must precede every other call
options.says: Ruled out because a client "is free to invoke any RPC inline", so discovery is optional.
